entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1
 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Revision Case No.1772 Of 2009
Judgment:
This Criminal Revision Case is filed by the petitioner aggrieved by the judgment dated 22.07.2009 in Crl.A.No.138 of 2007, on the file of I Additional Sessions Judge, at Khammam.

entities.text: I Additional Sessions Judge, at Khammam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the revision petitioner and learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent-State.
Perused the record.
3. The revision petitioner was convicted by the First Class Magistrate for the offence under Section 420 of IPC.
In fact, the case of the prosecution is that A-1 to A-4 have entered into a criminal conspiracy to cheat persons who wanted a job in Kothagudem Thermal Power Station (KTPS).
Accordingly, P.Ws.2, 3, 5, 10 and 11 deposed before the Court below that it was this petitioner/A-4 who collected money promising to provide jobs.
However, he had duped them.

The version of the above said witnesses was believed by the Court below and also the learned Sessions Judge concurred with the findings of the learned Magistrate when the conviction was carried in appeal.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the revision petitioner submits that the revision petitioner is a Class-IV employee working as a watchman and he does have the competence to get any jobs.
The prosecution failed to provide any documentary evidence such as any receipts for the payments made to A-4/revision petitioner.

P.W.10 had specifically stated that the promissory note was given by the revision petitioner, however, neither the promissory note nor any other details filed by P.W.1 were filed before the Court below.
P.W.4-who is another witness, though stated that he had taken money from his father, his father was not examined.
Collectively, there is no corroboration of the statements made by P.Ws.2, 3, 5, 9, 10 and 11 either oral or documentary to substantiate the case of the prosecution.

5. On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor submits that the findings of the Court below cannot be interfered since victims themselves have stated before the Court below that money was collected by the revision petitioner and cheated them.

6. The arguments of the legal aid counsel Mrs.P.Radhika cannot be accepted when the victims themselves who are P.Ws.2, 3, 5, 9, 10 and 11 have specifically stated before the Court below that they have given money and identified the petitioner as the person who had taken money on the promise of providing jobs.
There is no necessity for any corroboration to the evidence of the said witnesses.
The evidence of the said witnesses is believable and acceptable.

Thatikonda Satyanarayana, Khammam ... vs The State Of A.P., Rep. By P.P., ... on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23669404/
1 7.

entities.text: Thatikonda Satyanarayana, Khammam ... vs The State Of A.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said circumstances, there are no grounds to interfere with the conviction recorded by the Courts below.

However, it is submitted that there are no similar cases against the revision petitioner, he is aged above 60 years and suffering from old age ailments and since the case is of the year, 2007 and nearly 17 years have passed, this Court deems it appropriate to reduce the sentence of imprisonment to the period already undergone by the revision petitioner, while confirming the conviction.
8.
Accordingly, the Revision is partly allowed reducing the sentence of imprisonment to the period already undergone by the petitioner.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.

K.SURENDER, J Date: 11.06.2024 dv Thatikonda Satyanarayana, Khammam ... vs The State Of A.P., Rep. By P.P., ... on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23669404/
